evidence_proposals.excerpt_or_summary: Radde presents six kinds of deferred organisational work and a subjective influence map, and reports a team questioning and follow-up process.
Shein offers situated hypotheses about transfer of responsibilities and distinguishes recognising a problem from sustaining priority and action.
Velitchkov distinguishes discretion within a coordination arrangement from opportunities arising through participation, and proposes that control over coordination tends to concentrate.
De Visch asks which relationships sustain value creation and frames autonomy and cohesion in human-developmental terms.
Whitla distinguishes substantive meaning from the identity and belonging communicated by using or challenging a representation.
Workman presents an approach to testing conditions under which a strategy fails stakeholder goals, with assumptions open to challenge.
The article describes coordination control and counter-actions, and rejects concentration alone as an evidenced explanation of collapse.

profiles.title: The Second Law of Technodynamics
profiles.canonical_definition: An attributed proposal by Ivo Velitchkov concerning the concentration of control over coordination terms.
profiles.summary: Velitchkov proposes that coordination control tends to concentrate without counter-action. Control concerns the ability to set or change terms on which others depend and which they cannot readily replace. Counter-action can itself create another concentration.
profiles.why_it_matters: The proposal asks who can change participation terms, and what an effective alternative would require.
key_distinctions: Participatory discretion and the opportunities enabled by participation are distinct.
The thermodynamics comparison is a mnemonic, not a physical equivalence.
The full article does not establish concentration alone as a cause of collapse.
profiles.context_and_lineage: The SysCoI discovery record is retained. The conference account and two public articles provide a more detailed, attributed account.
common_misreadings: A proposed tendency is not a demonstrated universal law.
open_checks: Audio and on-screen visuals have not been independently checked against the auto-generated captions.
profiles.editorial_note: The older linked Productive Organisational Paradoxes deck is a different presentation. De Visch uses autonomy in a distinct human-developmental sense.
